text:
alex: Heads-up — AcmeCorp prod incident: they auto-upgraded to redwood-python 1.9.0 and started getting TypeError from our SDK. Customer sees 500s and a billing spike (retries). I grabbed logs & repro below.

carol: Ugh. Can you paste the error and repro steps? Any env details (python version, pip source)?

alex: 
- Python 3.10.8
- redwood-python 1.9.0 (pip install redwood==1.9.0)
- Error from their app: `TypeError: text_generation() got an unexpected keyword argument 'stream'`
- App code snippet (works on 1.8.x):
```
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_KEY"])
resp = c.text_generation(model="gpt-test", prompt=prompt, stream=True)
for chunk in resp:
    print(chunk.text)
```
- On 1.9.0 that raises the TypeError, then their app retries at service layer and we see repeated requests in logs (~100 reqs/min).

jordan: Thanks. I remember we changed the streaming API in 1.9.0 — `stream` was renamed to `response_mode` and now streaming returns an async iterator by default. We should have added compatibility shim.

maya: Confirmed. We intentionally changed signature to `text_generation(..., response_mode="sync|stream")` but neglected to accept `stream` as a deprecated alias. Also, we adjusted the default retry policy in the transport layer: backoff was shortened by mistake, so transient failures retried too aggressively. That explains the billing spike.

carol: Customer-facing asks: 1) quick workaround 2) ETA on fix 3) credits?

maya: Workaround: pin to last safe patch `pip install redwood==1.8.9` or update callsites: replace `stream=True` with `response_mode=\"stream\"` and iterate over the returned streaming object. Example: 
```
# migration
resp = c.text_generation(model="gpt-test", prompt=prompt, response_mode="stream")
for chunk in resp:
    print(chunk.text)
```
Patch ETA: I'll cut 1.9.1 today that restores a compatibility alias for `stream` and reverts the retry backoff to previous values. Release PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3421 (internal).

alex: Can we expedite a backport patch to 1.8.x that keeps new behavior but avoids the livelock? Customer asked for a non‑downgrade path.

maya: Backport won't help — the shim is tiny; I'll publish 1.9.1 with the alias and retry fix. It should be available in ~2–3 hours after CI. I will also add a runtime warning if `stream` is used so devs know to migrate.

jordan: Ops: we should also add a monitoring rule to detect sudden retry loop spikes per customer and auto-open CS ticket. Filing infra ticket.

sre-bot: Deploy notification: builds/3421 started (CI).

carol: For AcmeCorp: propose 1) ask them to pin to 1.8.9 immediately (command below) 2) we cut credits equivalent to duplicated requests while we patch 3) offer to join a short call to help migrate.
```
pip install 'redwood==1.8.9'
# or
pip install 'redwood==1.9.1'  # when released
```

alex: Sent the pin + credit offer. They want ETA — gave ~3h. Thx.

maya: CI green, publishing 1.9.1 now. It will include:
- compatibility alias for `stream` to `response_mode`
- retry backoff restored to previous schedule
- changelog & migration note in release notes

release-bot: Release 1.9.1 published: https://pypi.org/project/redwood/1.9.1 (internal)

alex: Customer upgraded to 1.9.1 and confirms errors gone. They accepted a small billing credit for duplicates.

jordan: Postmortem items: 1) stricter semver enforcement for minor vs patch; 2) pre-release smoke that runs major libraries against pinned internal apps; 3) include migration guide in changelog.

maya: I'll own the follow-ups and add a migration section to docs + an automated deprecation warning in the SDK.

carol: Thanks everyone. Closing loop with Acme. :thumbsup:
